{{For|medical procedure used to evaluate the upper gastrointestinal tract|Endoscopy}}
{{Short description|Mathematical group}}
In [[mathematics]], '''endoscopic groups''' of [[reductive algebraic group]]s were introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Robert |last=Langlands|authorlink=Robert Langlands|year1=1979|year2=1983}} in his work on the [[stable trace formula]].

Roughly speaking, an endoscopic group ''H'' of ''G'' is a [[quasi-split group]] whose [[Langlands dual|L-group]] is the connected component of the centralizer of a semisimple element of the L-group of ''G''.

In the [[stable trace formula]],  unstable [[orbital integral]]s on a  group ''G'' correspond to  stable orbital integrals on its endoscopic groups ''H''. The relation between them is given by the [[fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|fundamental lemma]].
